A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PB-SAC research work. All 28 pages of each version, including equations, figures, Table 1 and Appendices A–I, are readable and support reliable matching despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original MuJoCo experiments comparing PB-SAC with SAC and PBAC, together with certificate evaluations, sensitivity analyses and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendices G–H.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the specified control flow: v2 places critic adaptation outside the actor-frozen conditional, whereas v3 places it in the else branch, restricting adaptation to the frozen-actor phase. This aligns the pseudocode with the existing Section 4.4 description; the architecture and objectives remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate HalfCheetah, Ant, Hopper and Walker2d, including the same very-delayed-reward Ant scenario. No dataset, task or environmental coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: SAC and PBAC remain the evaluated comparators in the corresponding dense- and sparse-reward experiments. Comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes critic-adaptation sampling from 512 to 256 posterior samples. This corrects an inconsistency with v2's Section 4.4 and Table 1, which already specify 256. The PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The fixed-mixing-time sweep at 1, 50, 100, 300, 500 and 1000, adaptive-sampling and posterior-guided-exploration ablations, and KL-divergence diagnostic are retained with identical plots.

E5.justification: The plotted uncertainty bands and reporting practices are unchanged. Neither version supplies experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts or significance tests that are added or revised in the other.

E6.justification: The matched result graphics are identical: v2 Figures 1 and 4–8 correspond to v3 Figures 2 and 5–9. Performance, certificate and diagnostic results are retained; shortening Section 5.3's verbal summaries does not remove their underlying evidence.

T1.justification: v3 corrects the loss-expectation sign near Equation 8, adds a clipping-bias argument in Remark 3.1 and Appendix B.2, and explicitly establishes posterior-uniform quantification through the prior-averaged probability event in Appendix B.5.3. Appendix C adds the finite-grid union-bound penalty. These are localized refinements; Equation 13 and its rates remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction recasts the priority claim: v2 claims the first practical algorithm optimizing a non-vacuous PAC-Bayesian bound in modern deep RL; v3 specifies the first practical algorithm for SAC optimizing a PAC-Bayes bound. The headline certification and competitive-performance claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 4 newly distinguishes deployment safety from obstacle-avoidance Safe RL and interprets the certificate gap as evidence about deployment reliability. It also explains how posterior spread controls exploration. The conclusion removes the computational-overhead/scalability limitation and replaces its KL-instability discussion with a posterior-expressiveness concern.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 newly discloses softmax self-normalized importance sampling over standardized log-ratios. Sections 4.1 and 4.3 specify finite candidate evaluation through the critic and preservation of intact rollout trajectories. These additions document implementation details without establishing that the underlying implementation changed.

R1.justification: v3 adds Sutton and Barto (2018) for RL background and Xu et al. (2022) for trustworthy-RL positioning. The substantive comparisons with previous PAC-Bayesian RL research remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 edits prose and cross-references, expands selected explanations, rewrites the conclusion and adds an Impact Statement. The principal section sequence and Appendices A–I are retained, so the narrative changes remain localized.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from single-column to two-column conference formatting, with redesigned front matter, running headers and extensively repositioned displays. The appendix algorithm diagram gains timing annotations and is also displayed in the introduction as Figure 1. Existing result graphics and Table 1 are resized and repositioned.

improvement.justification: v3 improves precision and reproducibility by correcting the loss identity, clarifying the posterior-uniform proof, repairing Algorithm 1's branching and reconciling the adaptation-sample count. These concrete gains are limited by unchanged empirical evidence, removal of the scalability caveat, and Appendix B.2's unsupported extension of clipping conservatism to softmax self-normalized weights. Overall, the corrections provide a modest quality improvement without fully resolving the certificate's implementation-level justification.
